# hullBase

**Baseline correction for FTIR spectra using a refined rubberband method**

hullBase is an R package for baseline correction of spectra such as Fourier
transform infrared (FTIR) spectra. It builds the plain rubberband baseline
(the lower convex hull of the spectrum) and then refines only the hull
segments that hide a concave region of the background. Where to refine is
decided by a threshold calculated from the noise level of the spectrum, and
how strongly to refine is calculated from the estimated height of the concave
region. The peak width is set by the user.

## Key features

* Rubberband baseline from the lower convex hull, computed in C++
* Input checks with a clear message for each problem
* Noise estimation and detection of hull segments that hide a concave region
* Local refinement of only those segments, other segments keep the rubberband
* One result object, `BaselineModel`, with `print()`, `summary()` and `plot()` methods
* `simulate_spectrum()` for test spectra with a known true baseline

## Installation

hullBase is not on CRAN. Install the development version from GitHub.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ThanyaManivannan/hullBase", build_vignettes = TRUE)
```

Installing from GitHub compiles C++ code, which on Windows needs
[Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/).

## Quick start

A simulated spectrum is used here because its true baseline is known.

```{r example}
library(hullBase)

set.seed(1)
sim <- simulate_spectrum(baseline = "concave", snr_db = 30)

fit <- correct(sim, peak_width = 300)
fit
```

`peak_width` is the width, in the units of `x`, of the widest peak or group
of overlapping peaks.

```{r summary}
summary(fit)
```

## Example result

```{r plot-baseline}
plot(fit)
```

The plain rubberband runs straight under the concave background. The
refined baseline follows it, and the refined segment is shaded.

```{r plot-corrected}
plot(fit, which = "corrected")
```

After correction the spectrum lies at zero between the peaks.

```{r error}
c(rubberband = sqrt(mean((fit$rubberband - sim$baseline)^2)),
  hullBase   = sqrt(mean((fit$baseline   - sim$baseline)^2)))
```

Root mean squared error against the true baseline, for this one spectrum.

## Input and output

* **Input**, two numeric vectors `x` and `y`, or a data frame with columns `x` and `y`
* **`x`**, wavenumbers, each value once, roughly even spacing, any order
* **`y`**, absorbance, peaks pointing upwards, no `NA`, `NaN` or `Inf`
* **Main setting**, `peak_width`, in the units of `x`
* **Output**, a `BaselineModel` object with fields `x`, `y`, `baseline`,
  `corrected`, `rubberband`, `noise`, `peak_width`, `method`, `segments` and `call`
* **Methods**, `print()`, `summary()` and `plot()`

`correct(x, y, method = "rubberband")` returns the plain rubberband
baseline for comparison.

## Functions

* `correct()` runs the full correction and returns a `BaselineModel`
* `lower_hull()` gives the plain rubberband baseline
* `noise_estimate()` gives the noise level of a spectrum
* `detect_concave_segments()` finds the hull segments that hide a concave region
* `refine_segment()` refines one segment so the baseline follows the concave region
* `simulate_spectrum()` makes a test spectrum with a known true baseline

## How well it works

Mean RMSE against the true baseline over 20 simulated spectra for each row,
`peak_width = 300`, with `set.seed(2026)` set once before all 300 spectra
were simulated.

```{r results-table, echo = FALSE}
data.frame(
  shape      = c("concave", "concave", "mixed", "mixed", "flat", "linear", "convex"),
  snr_db     = c(30, 20, 30, 20, 30, 30, 30),
  rubberband = c(0.745, 0.895, 0.787, 0.904, 0.089, 0.086, 0.057),
  hullBase   = c(0.056, 0.223, 0.069, 0.204, 0.089, 0.086, 0.057)
)
```

The error falls on concave and mixed baselines. Flat, linear and convex
baselines are unchanged because no segment is refined. These results apply
to the package simulator with Gaussian peaks, and have not been established
for all measured spectra.

## Documentation

* User guide, `vignette("hullBase")`
* Help pages, for example `?correct` and `?simulate_spectrum`
* Measured example spectra used in testing are loaded from other packages
  and are not shipped with hullBase. SrE.IR comes from
  [ChemoSpec](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ChemoSpec) and paracetamol
  from [hyperSpec](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=hyperSpec).
* Source code and issues, <https://github.com/ThanyaManivannan/hullBase>

## Limitations

* `peak_width` is chosen by the user, and a peak wider than it is treated as background
* A concave region lower than about 7.6 noise standard deviations is not found on the simulated spectra
* The baseline is made of straight pieces and is not smooth
* The lowest noise points pull the baseline slightly below the true baseline
* Noise is assumed to be the same size across the spectrum
* Repeated wavenumbers stop the correction, and transmittance must be
  converted to absorbance, A = log10(1/T), before calling `correct()`
* Only Gaussian peaks were evaluated, so Lorentzian peaks have not been tested
* The noise estimate assumes the noise is independent between neighbouring
  points, so smoothed or interpolated spectra may give a wrong noise level
